about: Sign-offs for the release gate (edakit gate). Each one counts only for the hash of its scope: 'circuit' = state_sha256 (graph, parts database, simulation config), 'layout' = layout_sha256 (board files with their artwork, footprint geometry), 'fab' = fab_sha256 (what the manufacturer builds from: Gerber layers rasterised, drill hits, BOM and CPL rows – in the protocol header of a gate run with stage F). When something there changes, it no longer counts – copy the new hash from the protocol header after the check was repeated. phase: 'export' blocks the release, 'order' and 'acceptance' come after the export. An accepted warning with scope 'decision' counts regardless of the hash and refers to a numbered decision in the docs. Parts are signed in their parts entry (field 'verified').

manual.text: Critical parts (BT1, D1) checked a second time against the datasheet, independently – the agent electrical-reviewer in its own session
manual.note: M-1: OK for state a2a6ed922953794c6e583f2b9ec73955cda601ec937db605d2376b7969096047; requirements met: R-2. Changed from 48984185: the accept of HINT.debounce left the graph (edakit no longer reports it without an MCU reading SW1); the cell states fresh and used got i_max_a 3 mA and LIM.i/cell is accepted on BT1 with D-7 – its reason checked against Jauch CR 2032 H2B (15092025, sha256 bf0267b6…): 3 mA continuous, 15 mA pulse, pulse curve 300 Ω for 5 s; SW1 held gives 10.7 mA fresh, 6.3 mA used, about 12 mA from a brand-new cell at 3.4 V, a single primary cell run flat comes to no harm. edakit's new LIM.p holds D1 at 14.8 mW against 32.5 mW. BT1 and D1 against their signed datasheets (sha256 760a7d67…, 3a6caf35…): pinout, polarity at the footprint (BT1 pad 1 '+' on VBAT, D1 pad 1 cathode on GND), ratings. R-2: with SW1 released about 0.03 µA through SW1's insulation (≥ 100 MΩ). R-1 by its rows (1.22 mA) and D-2. Note taken over: the used cell's assumed 40 Ω is low by Jauch's pulse curve (the row falls below 1 mA from about 90 Ω) – R-1 rests on D-2's argument.

manual.text: Regulatory review: circuit and parts against EU law for the purpose in the graph – the agent regulatory-reviewer in its own session. No finding 'block' open. Support, not legal advice: no claim to correctness, nothing legally guaranteed
manual.note: M-6: OK for state a2a6ed922953794c6e583f2b9ec73955cda601ec937db605d2376b7969096047 and purpose private. Changed since 48984185: the accept of HINT.debounce removed from the graph (no regulatory content), and the cell states' i_max_a 3 mA with LIM.i/cell accepted on BT1 (D-7) – a question of capacity, not of safety: 10.7 mA at most while SW1 is held, a few mW in R1, D1 and the cell, a single cell drained without hazard. Purpose and parts unchanged. Notes, none blocking: who uses it (settled by D-5), a board given away is a gift with a new M-6, the parts' RoHS/REACH statements open (no duty for private), board and cell to separate collection at end of life. Not legal advice – support without any claim to correctness; nothing here is legally guaranteed.

manual.text: Layout reviewed independently (manufacturability, mechanics, operation, looks) on the manufacturing files of a gate run with this layout – e.g. by the agent pcb-reviewer. No finding 'block' open, every 'important' finding fixed or rejected by the owner
manual.note: M-5: OK for fab f958da9ad4f85a2eb6376122c5ec21203dbbc12730c1ca59184b383f90a61d70; layout 1f529013a56fea12747977d89132f5f3822c9562158d49190e9769a74420b338. Manufacturing files of gate run 20261031-130109 against 20261031-115405: only the top silkscreen and the order settings changed. JLCPCB manufacturability including the round outline with two own tooling holes, copper 91/93 % without floating copper, the cell's overhang strips and 10 mm lever room free, BT1's tabs within reach of the iron, D1 visible beside SW1; the BT1 designator and the centred board label clear of the cell, the pads and the edge; order.md states the two tooling holes as 'Added by Customer'.

manual.text: At JLCPCB after the upload: assembly preview – rotation and polarity of every polarised part (compare with polarity_<board>.png); BOM without missing parts; price
Acceptance test of every delivered board: visual check (BT1 and D1 the right way round), D1 lights while SW1 is pressed and is dark once it is released
